topic: Design vocabulary for non-US, non-CS academic personal sites (Europe, Asia, Australia) plus a hard look at the Indian academic web baseline — aimed at a hydrologist/hydroclimatologist at IIT Hyderabad. ~48 sites fetched and inspected at the HTML/CSS level (fonts, palettes, nav, viewport, template signatures) plus rendered reads.
key_findings: IIT Hyderabad's own brand system is unusually good and is the correct anchor to extend. Verified in the inline <style> of https://www.iith.ac.in/ce/satishr/: self-hosted Frutiger LT Pro (Roman/Light/Bold/Black/Italic .otf), body background #FDFBF8 (warm off-white, NOT white), body text #333333, accent amber #D97706 with the button orange #fa9110 (from https://iith.ac.in/assets/css/rtm-custom.css), plus brick #d1402a and slate #0f172a/#475569. Built on Tailwind. A personal site that uses a warm off-white ground + a humanist sans + an amber/brick accent will read as 'of IITH' without looking like the IITH template.

The Indian institutional baseline is literally un-designed Bootstrap 3. IIT Delhi (home.iitd.ac.in) and IISc (iisc.ac.in) both still ship Bootstrap 3 with Glyphicons and the unbranded default link blue #337ab7; IIT Bombay (iitb.ac.in) has no type system at all (font-family: 'Segoe UI', Tahoma, Geneva, Verdana). Any deliberate typographic decision is already a visible step above the field.

Word-export personal pages are still normal at the very top of the field. https://www.civil.iitb.ac.in/~subimal/ (Subimal Ghosh, Institute Chair Professor, IIT Bombay) contains `content="Microsoft Word 15"` and `urn:schemas-microsoft-com` namespaces with font-family values of `roman`/`swiss`/`Calibri`, and has NO viewport meta tag. http://personal.lse.ac.uk/ghatak/ (Maitreesh Ghatak, LSE) is the same genre (`default.files/image002.jpg`, no viewport). Even https://gabriel-zucman.eu/ (one of the most-cited living economists) runs a 2011-era WordPress 'hybrid' theme with no viewport meta. Non-responsive is common — which means responsiveness alone differentiates, but is not a design.

The free-template failure mode, verified in the wild at an IIT: https://akshayanikumbh.github.io/ (IIT Bombay, Atmospheric Convection and Dynamics Group) carries the exact HTML5 UP asset signature (assets/js/jquery.scrollex.min.js, jquery.scrolly.min.js, breakpoints.min.js, util.js, assets/css/noscript.css) AND still ships the template's placeholder copy: an <h2> reading 'And this is a massive headline', a news item titled 'NCAR CAS visit interdum dolor', 'Tempus sed nulla imperdiet', and images pic04.jpg–pic07.jpg. This is precisely the smell the new site must avoid.

Google Sites under an institutional Workspace domain can silently become sign-in-walled. https://sites.google.com/a/iitgn.ac.in/water-and-climate-change/home (Vimal Mishra's old lab site) returns a Google Drive 'Sign in' page to an anonymous fetch — 1.24 MB of Google auth UI, not content. Same for https://sites.google.com/iitgn.ac.in/uditbhatia. Strong argument for owning the domain and serving static HTML, with Google Docs/Sheets used only as the private editing surface.

Neither satishregonda.in nor raftwaters.in currently resolves. `dig @1.1.1.1` returns no A record and no NS for either (control: iith.ac.in → 103.232.241.56 with dns1/dns2.iith.ac.in). DNS/hosting still has to be stood up; raftwaters.in is not live today, so the RAFT page on the new site is currently the only public RAFT presence.

The best Indian model for a hydro/climate PI's IA is Vimal Mishra's Water & Climate Lab (React SPA at http://vmishra.people.iitgn.ac.in/water&climate/). Routes extracted from its JS bundle: /research/{climate-and-urban-systems, climate-extremes-understanding, hydrologic-monitoring-and-prediction, hydrologic-sensitivity-and-change}; /publications/{journal-articles, books-expository-and-review-articles, conference-presentations, invited-papers}; /people/{current, alumni, interns, gallery}; and — importantly — first-class /data and /data-portals. Its weakness: FIVE font families in main.ca611b17.css (Maven Pro, Work Sans, Jost, Source Sans Pro, Open Sans) over #003b75/#00aeef, which is what makes it read templated.

Roxy Mathew Koll (IITM Pune, https://www.climate.rocksea.org/) names research areas as findings, not categories: 'Increasing Arabian Sea Cyclones', 'Warm pool expansion warps MJO', 'Marine Heatwaves and Monsoon', 'Widespread Extreme Rains', 'Monsoon Droughts', 'Climate and Dengue', 'Future Indian Ocean'. Nav also promotes 'Data Products' and 'Student Guidelines' to top level. His news wall is built from scanned newspaper op-ed clippings — Hindustan Times, Indian Express, Eenadu (Telugu), Mathrubhumi, Samana — a credibility device that is specifically Indian and impossible to fake.

HydroSense Lab, IIT Delhi (https://hydrosense.iitd.ac.in/) is the closest peer to what Satish needs: Montserrat 400/500/700 + Open Sans on the 'Academix' WP theme, near-monochrome black/#EDF2F6 with ONE red accent #D30015, four research areas as image cards ('Hydrologic Modeling and Forecasting', 'Geospatial Artificial Intelligence', 'Climate Change Impacts', plus lab infrastructure), and a funder logo strip immediately under the hero (ISRO, MoES, MoRD, DST, PSA, CDRI, IC-IMPACTS, Sony). Caveat: its TLS chain is incomplete — `openssl s_client` gives 'Verify return code: 21 (unable to verify the first certificate)' and Claude's fetcher refused it outright, though curl -L works. Institutional subdomains are a real hosting risk in India.

Using your own paper/model figures AS the visual identity is the strongest anti-generic move, and the best examples are non-US. https://global-hydrodynamics.github.io/ (Dai Yamazaki, IIS, University of Tokyo) runs its entire hero slider on its own outputs: /images/slider/MERIT_DEM.jpg, MERIT_width.jpg, CaMa_Mekong.jpg, CaMa_model.jpg, Hillslope.jpg. Ed Hawkins (Reading) went further at https://www.climate-lab-book.ac.uk/ — two of his own figures, 'Climate spirals' and 'Warming stripes', are permanent top-level NAV ITEMS, and one spun off into its own site https://showyourstripes.info/.

Wageningen (https://www.wur.nl/en.htm) has the single most useful institutional palette for a water/environment site: cream grounds #FBF6E5 and #F3ECD3, deep greens #004D00 and #153816, navy #002B47, dark red #661118. Warm, earthy, agrarian — and conspicuously not corporate blue. This is a far better starting point for a hydrologist than the default 'water = cyan' reflex.

Named institutional typefaces, all verified from live CSS: ETH Zurich = DINPro (blue #215caf, dark #08407e, red #e2001a); TU Delft = Roboto Slab Light/Regular/Medium as the brand face (cyan #00a6d6, navy #0C2340/#1c1c73, green #a5ca1a); TU Munich = STIX Two Text serif + Roboto (#3070B3, #072140); KTH = Figtree (navy #000061, #004791, #007fae); Imperial College = ImperialText-VF variable font with near-black #161a1d and a deliberately electric secondary set (#0000cd, #c71585, #00ff7f, #40e0d0); Cambridge = Lato + Open Sans (magenta #e5007d, yellow #f9cd02); Tsinghua = Source Sans Pro + 微软雅黑 (purple #791cb5); U Tokyo = Noto Sans JP + Roboto (navy #06355b, gold #f6b506); Melbourne 'Find an Expert' = Fraunces variable serif (opsz/SOFT/WONK axes) + Source Sans Pro, navy #003c55.

Our World in Data (Oxford / Global Change Data Lab, https://ourworldindata.org/) is the reference implementation of a data-forward system: ONE family, Lato, self-hosted in eight weights plus italics (Hairline, Light, Regular, Medium, Bold, Heavy, Black), over a tinted navy scale #1d3d63 → #426591 → #577291 → #a4b6ca → #dbe5f0 with a single red #ce261e. One family + many weights + one hue scale + one accent is directly buildable and never reads as a template.

Editorial-magazine treatment, verified in CSS rather than vibes: https://www.ayonadatta.com/ (Ayona Datta, UCL human geography, urban India) loads Playfair Display via Adobe Typekit and its custom.css does the real work — 1.5px solid #000 bottom rules instead of input boxes, uppercase micro-labels at letter-spacing .1em–.2em, 2px solid #000 ghost buttons that invert on hover, navy #16263c. Squarespace underneath, but the overrides make it look art-directed.

Quarto now produces sites that look bespoke. https://cecibaldoni.github.io/ is `quarto-1.10.18` and its home page is a hand-drawn SVG cityscape (img/ceci-city.svg) whose buildings ARE the navigation — icons for research, illustrations, talks-workshops, open-science, bookshop, radio, van, coffee-kiosk. Palette: cream #fdf6ee, forest #0f3318, gold #e8c97e, sage #a3be6e; Roboto Mono. Proof that a static generator plus one commissioned illustration beats any premium theme.

In map-heavy fields the artefact is the design. https://www.dannydorling.org/ leads every news item with a 'Featured_graphic' image (Featured_graphic-5.png, FeaturedGraphic-1-1024x653.jpg) — a map or chart, never a portrait — with Lora serif headings over Muli/Roboto UI. https://www.statsmapsnpix.com/ (Alasdair Rae, ex-Sheffield geography) is a plain Blogger blog where every single post thumbnail is a square 400×400 map; the maps carry it entirely.

'Indian and modern' does not have to mean 'imported'. Azim Premji University (https://azimpremjiuniversity.edu.in/) runs Source Sans 3 variable (200–900, with italics) on Tailwind over ochre #c76815, deep maroon #771d1d and cream #fef6d6 — warm, sub-continental, unmistakably contemporary. Krea (https://krea.edu.in/) uses Manrope + Merriweather over #005DA6/#103450/#1099D6.

Do not model the department page. ETH's own Rietholzbach research-catchment page (https://iac.ethz.ch/group/land-climate-dynamics/research/rietholzbach.html) — one of the most famous instrumented catchments in Europe — has no photographs, no map and no data plot at all, just prose and 'More information about…' links. European institutional CMSs are deliberately dry; the personal site is the only place the field photos and figures can live.

Bilingual structure is normal in Asia and worth borrowing. https://aqua.t.u-tokyo.ac.jp/en/ (River and Environmental Engineering Lab, UTokyo — Oki lineage) runs EN/JA through WPML and puts the Japanese research statement in the <title>. The Indian analogue for Satish's urban-flood and water-awareness work would be a Telugu-language outreach page — locally credible, internationally legible, and something no template ships with.
recommendations: Anchor the palette on IITH's own warm off-white #FDFBF8 (not #FFF) with #333333 text, and pick ONE accent. Two defensible directions, both verified in the wild: (a) IITH-native — amber #D97706 / #fa9110 with brick #d1402a for links and rules; (b) Wageningen-style water-and-land — cream #FBF6E5 ground, deep green #153816 headings, navy #002B47, one dark red #661118 for emphasis. Avoid cyan-blue 'water' clichés; TU Delft's #00a6d6 and Divi's #2ea3f2 are what everyone else already looks like.

Use exactly one typeface family in many weights, Our World in Data style, plus at most one display face. A humanist sans in the Frutiger lineage keeps continuity with IITH's licensed Frutiger LT Pro without licensing it — practical open options: Inter, Source Sans 3 (as APU uses), Figtree (as KTH uses), or Lato (as OWID uses). If a second face is wanted, make it a real editorial serif for the essay/blog body only (Fraunces, as Melbourne uses, or STIX Two Text, as TUM uses). Hard cap: two families. Vimal Mishra's lab site shows what five families do.

Make Satish's own figures the visual system. Pick 4–6 images that are exclusively his group's output — a Godavari/Musi streamflow hydrograph, an urban-flood inundation map of Hyderabad, a SnapFlood screenshot, a monsoon-anomaly map, a drone frame, a rain-gauge/field photo — and use them as the ONLY imagery above the fold and as the research-area cards. That is the Yamazaki Lab move (MERIT_DEM.jpg, CaMa_Mekong.jpg as hero) and the Ed Hawkins move (figure promoted to nav item). Ban stock photography entirely — even ayonadatta.com is weakened by an unsplash hero.

Name the research areas as claims, not categories. Follow Roxy Koll ('Increasing Arabian Sea Cyclones', 'Warm pool expansion warps MJO') rather than 'Hydrology / Climate Change'. For Satish, e.g. 'Forecasting the Godavari at 7–15 days', 'Why Hyderabad floods', 'Building India's missing hydrologic record', 'Monsoon variability and reservoir decisions'. Each gets one page, one own-figure, one paragraph of plain English, and a list of the papers behind it.

Adopt Vimal Mishra's IA as the skeleton, since it is already proven for an Indian hydro-climate PI, and simplify: Home / Research (4 named themes) / Publications (journal · reviews & books · conference · invited) / Data & Products (SnapFlood, hydrologic database, dashboards) / People (current · alumni · interns · gallery) / Teaching / RAFT / Blog / Contact. Keep 'Data & Products' at top level — it is what distinguishes an operational hydrologist from a paper-writer, and it maps directly to his existing 'Products & Publications' page.

Put a funder/collaborator logo strip immediately under the hero, as HydroSense does (ISRO, MoES, MoRD, DST, PSA, CDRI). For Satish that means NOAA/National Weather Service, the World Bank, Johns Hopkins, IIT Kanpur, CU Boulder, plus current Indian funders. It is the fastest, most honest international-credibility signal available, and it is content he already has.

Steal Roxy Koll's press wall, including regional-language clippings. A 'In the press' strip of newspaper mastheads (The Hindu, Deccan Chronicle, Eenadu/Sakshi in Telugu) with date + outlet + link, driven from a Google Sheet, is high-signal in India, invisible to template-detectors, and trivially editable by a non-technical professor.

Add a 'For students' page in the manner of Koll's 'Student Guidelines' — how to apply, what he expects, what a PhD in the group looks like, prerequisites (R/Shiny, GEE, statistics — all already listed on his current site). It converts a dead 'Opportunities' link into the most-visited page on most PI sites and reads as generous rather than promotional.

Consider a Telugu-language page for the urban-flood / water-awareness work. Nobody's template has it, it is locally accurate (Hyderabad flooding is a Telangana public-interest issue), and it follows the established EN/JA pattern at UTokyo's aqua lab. Even a single translated page signals that the outreach is real.

Do not host on an institutional subdomain. hydrosense.iitd.ac.in serves an incomplete certificate chain (openssl verify code 21) and was refused outright by an automated fetcher; iith.ac.in path-hosting means URL churn. Serve satishregonda.in from a static host with automatic certs, and set up DNS first — neither satishregonda.in nor raftwaters.in resolves today.

Ship responsive from line one and treat it as table stakes, not a feature. Of the ~48 sites inspected, the ones with NO viewport meta at all were subimal (IITB), ghatak (LSE), zucman (PSE), statsmapsnpix, iiserb's CGMLI lab, gramaziokohler and the older IISc pages. Wide content on a hydrology site — publication tables, long DOI strings, wide figures — must scroll inside its own container, never the page body.

Build the RAFT page as a rich single scroll with its own accent tint drawn from the same palette (a shifted hue, not a second brand), an own-figure hero, the team grid, and a single prominent outbound link to raftwaters.in. Since raftwaters.in is currently dark, this page is the group's public face today — write it to stand alone.

Use an editorial detail set rather than card-and-shadow UI: hairline rules instead of boxes, uppercase micro-labels at 0.12em tracking for section eyebrows and figure captions, a monospace-numeral treatment for years/DOIs in the publication list, and generous measure (~62–68ch) on prose. That is the ayonadatta.com/OWID register and it costs nothing to implement.

For the blog, design the post page before the index: a real 'article' template with a figure-with-caption component and a pull-quote, because a hydrologist's posts will be figure-led (flood event post-mortems, forecast verification, monsoon commentary). Danny Dorling's 'featured graphic per post' pattern — image first, headline second — is the right index model.
details:
## Method

~48 URLs fetched with `curl -L` (real user-agent) into a scratch dir, then parsed for `<title>`, Google Fonts links, `font-family` declarations, `@font-face` names and font file names, hex-colour frequency, CSS custom properties, `<nav>` contents, headings, image paths, `<meta name=generator>`, script/stylesheet sources, and presence of `<meta name="viewport">`. Linked stylesheets were followed one level deep for typography/palette. Several sites additionally read in rendered form. DNS checked with `dig @1.1.1.1`; TLS with `openssl s_client`.

Scratch dir: `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-divyanshpandey-Desktop-Projects-Satish-Portfolio/0a1055f9-5c56-40cc-9342-e71706b18fa9/scratchpad/` (probe.sh, fonts.sh, sites/*.html).

---

## A. The client's current situation (verified)

**Existing Google Site** `https://sites.google.com/iith.ac.in/satishregonda/home` — nav: Home / Education & Employment / Products & Publications / Research (→ Urban Flood, SnapFlood, Guidelines for Sixer Twitter) / Teaching / Students / RAFT / Opportunities. Home text: Associate Professor, Hydraulics & Water Resources Engineering, Civil Engineering + Climate Change, IIT Hyderabad. MTech IIT Kanpur, PhD CU Boulder; NOAA National Weather Service (Washington DC), World Bank, Johns Hopkins; IITH since Feb 2017. Stated focus: "developing efficient solutions/tools that makes human life better at both short- and long-time scales", currently Urban Flood Modeling. Interests listed: hydrologic database development in India, hydroclimatologic processes under changing regimes, water awareness, hydrologic forecasting, decision-support products, urban climate, statistics, R, Shiny, drones, Google Earth Engine. One image only (a repeated header logo). Phone +91-40-2301 6315.

**IITH departmental profile** `https://www.iith.ac.in/ce/satishr/` lists Research Interests as: Urban and Rural Flood Modeling; Climate Sciences; Data Sciences; Statistical Modeling Techniques; Ensemble Forecasting; Multiscale Modelling; AI/ML; Climate Change. Office B-212. Note the two lists differ — the new site should reconcile them into 4 named themes.

**DNS:** `dig +short @1.1.1.1 satishregonda.in A` → empty; `NS` → empty. Same for `raftwaters.in`. Control `iith.ac.in` → `103.232.241.56`, NS `dns1/dns2.iith.ac.in`. Both target domains are unconfigured as of this check.

**IITH brand tokens** (from inline `<style>` on the profile page and `/assets/css/rtm-custom.css`):
```
@font-face { font-family:"FrutigerLTPro"; src:url("/assets/fonts/frutiger/FrutigerLTPro-Roman.otf") ... }
   + Light, Bold (700), Black (800), Italic (400 italic)
body { font-family:"FrutigerLTPro", Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif;
       background-color:#FDFBF8; color:#333333; }
.btn-iith { background-color:#fa9110; border-color:#fa9110; color:#fff; }
```
Other tokens seen on the page: `#D97706` (amber-600), `#0f172a`, `#475569`, `#f1f5f9`, `#cbd5e1`, `#94a3b8`, `#d1402a`. Stack: Tailwind + Alpine.js + Chart.js + Font Awesome 6.5.1. IITH is genuinely the best-branded of the Indian institutes I inspected.

---

## B. Indian baseline — what "typical" actually looks like

| Site | Stack / type | Palette | Viewport meta |
|---|---|---|---|
| `home.iitd.ac.in` | Bootstrap 3 + Glyphicons + FontAwesome | default `#337ab7`, IITD red `#B80F0A`, `#ffff00` | yes |
| `iisc.ac.in` | Bootstrap 3 + Glyphicons; Playfair Display, Roboto Condensed, Source Sans Pro, museo-sans all mixed | default `#337ab7`, `#108896` | yes |
| `www.iitb.ac.in` | no system; `'Segoe UI', Tahoma, Geneva, Verdana` | `#EEFBFF` | yes |
| `civil.iitb.ac.in/~subimal/` | **Microsoft Word 15 "Save as Web Page"** (`urn:schemas-microsoft-com`, `font-family: roman/swiss/Calibri`, `DV_Divya`) | `#4472C4`, `#1F3763` (Word theme colours) | **none** |
| `akshayanikumbh.github.io` | HTML5 UP template signature; **leftover lorem** ("And this is a massive headline", "NCAR CAS visit interdum dolor", pic04–07.jpg) | — | yes |
| `home.iiserb.ac.in/~kumarp/` (CGMLI Lab) | hand-rolled; single teal `#228878` (45 occurrences) | `#228878` | **none** |
| `hydrosense.iitd.ac.in` | WP + "Academix" theme + Elementor 3.28; Montserrat 400/500/700 + Open Sans | `#000`/`#EDF2F6` + one red `#D30015` | yes |
| `msaharia.com` | WP 6.1 + Elementor 3.13; Poppins 600 + Quicksand 400/600 | `--primary: rgb(224,107,109)`, `--secondary: rgb(64,137,110)`, `--tertiary: rgb(255,247,247)` | yes |
| `vmishra.people.iitgn.ac.in/water&climate/` | React SPA (CRA build) | `#003b75`, `#00aeef` | yes |
| `climate.rocksea.org` | WordPress + Autoptimize | sage `#bdcc96` dominant | yes |
| `azimpremjiuniversity.edu.in` | Tailwind + Source Sans 3 variable | ochre `#c76815`, maroon `#771d1d`, cream `#fef6d6` | yes |
| `krea.edu.in` | WP/Elementor; Manrope + Merriweather + Inter | `#005DA6`, `#103450`, `#1099D6` | yes |
| `iihs.co.in` | legacy; no font system | `#163959`, `#bd2426`, `#9bca3e`, `#2f7bbf` | yes |

**Vimal Mishra lab IA, extracted from `static/js/main.441d092f.js`:**
```
/research/climate-and-urban-systems
/research/climate-extremes-understanding
/research/hydrologic-monitoring-and-prediction
/research/hydrologic-sensitivity-and-change
/publications/journal-articles
/publications/books-expository-and-review-articles
/publications/conference-presentations
/publications/invited-papers
/people/current   /people/alumni   /people/interns   /people/gallery
/data   /data-portals   /news   /contact
```
CSS fonts in `main.ca611b17.css`: Maven Pro, Open Sans, Source Sans Pro, Work Sans, plus `@import` of Jost — five families.

**HydroSense nav:** Home / Research / Team / Publications / Products / Awards & Impact / News. H2s on home: "We Develop Technologies for Monitoring and Mitigating Natural Hazards" → "Dr. Manabendra Saharia" → "Lab Funded by" (logo strip) → "Lab Updates" → four research-area cards → "HydroSense Lab Infrastructure". Funder logos in `/wp-content/uploads/`: ISRO, MoRD, MoES, sonylogo, ICIMPACTS, PSA, DST, CDRI-logo. TLS: `Verify return code: 21 (unable to verify the first certificate)`; issuer GlobalSign RSA OV SSL CA 2018, CN=*.iitd.ac.in — intermediate not served.

**Roxy Koll nav (full):** Home / People (People @ Climate Lab, Roxy Mathew Koll, Student Guidelines) / Publications / Research (Data Products, Climate and Dengue, Future Indian Ocean, El Niño La Niña and the Monsoon, Marine Heatwaves and Monsoon, Indian Ocean Cyclones, Increasing Arabian Sea Cyclones, Warm pool expansion warps MJO, Widespread Extreme Rains, Marine Ecosystem changes, Monsoon Droughts, …). Home H1 "Events and Highlights 2025-2026"; H2s: Climate Research Lab / Student Guidelines / News Highlights / Gallery. News images are literally scanned press pages: `SuperElNino_OpEd_HindustanTimes_RoxyKoll_27Jul2026-scaled.png`, `SuperElNino_EditorialInterview_Eenadu_RoxyKoll_24Jul2026-scaled.png`, `Mathrubhumi_News_Edit_10Jul2026-scaled.jpg`, `India_Disaster_Drill_TheIndianExpress_2Aug2026.png`, `PathwaysSchool_Session_18Aug2026.png`. Tagline on the page: *"We put the ocean in a /shell/ and throw that shell back into the ocean."*

---

## C. Non-US, non-CS exemplar detail

**Yamazaki Lab (U Tokyo)** — `https://global-hydrodynamics.github.io/`, GitHub Pages + Bootstrap, `/css/main.css`. Home H1 "Welcome!", H2s: "What is Global Hydrodynamics?" → "Monthly Public Seminar" → "CaMa-Flood modelling community" → "Rainfall-Runoff Modelling Game" → "(In Japanese)". Slider = `MERIT_width.jpg`, `CaMa_Mekong.jpg`, `CaMa_model.jpg`, `MERIT_DEM.jpg`, `Hillslope.jpg`; team photo `DLab_2024Dec.jpg`. Rendered read: "carousel features research outputs rather than abstract imagery — topographic data visualisations, model outputs, DEM representations". A "Rainfall-Runoff Modelling Game" as a top-level home section is a memorable, non-generic outreach device.

**Climate Lab Book (Ed Hawkins, Reading)** — `https://www.climate-lab-book.ac.uk/`. Nav: Home / Climate spirals / Warming stripes / Visualisation resources / Comparing CMIP5 & observations / About / Contact. Two of his own figures are permanent nav items. Spin-off `https://showyourstripes.info/` (Vue + Vuetify, Roboto, greys `#424242`/`#e0e0e0`) exists purely to distribute one figure.

**Danny Dorling (Oxford)** — `https://www.dannydorling.org/`. WP "mesmerize-pro". Fonts: Lora (Georgia fallback) for the H1 and headings, Muli for UI, Roboto secondary. Accent `#ff1f55`/`#FF3369`. Every news card leads with `Featured_graphic-*.png` / `FeaturedGraphic-*.jpg`. H2s: News / Recent Books / What other people say. The "What other people say" section (pull-quotes about him) is a nice alternative to a self-written bio.

**Alasdair Rae** — `https://www.statsmapsnpix.com/`. Blogger, Open Sans, `#160` green links, `#444444` text, `#3778cd` accent. Every post thumbnail is a 400×400 map (`green-belt-pop-2021.png`, `building-area-vs-pop.png`, `uprn-vs-buildings.png`). No viewport meta — and still one of the most-read geography blogs. Content over chrome, but do not copy the missing responsiveness.

**Ayona Datta (UCL)** — `https://www.ayonadatta.com/`, Squarespace + Adobe Typekit. `font-family:'Playfair Display'`. Custom CSS: `.field-list .field-element { border-bottom: solid 1.5px #000; border-left/right/top: none; background: transparent; }`, `.form-button-wrapper .button { letter-spacing:.2em; font-weight:600; border:2px solid #000; background:none }` inverting to black on hover, `.form-title { text-transform:uppercase; letter-spacing:.1em }`, back-to-top button `#16263c`. Nav: About / Research / Speaking (Keynotes, Multimedia, Media & Press, Upcoming Talks) / Writing (Books, Journal Articles and Book Chapters, Op-eds, Reports, Blog) / Awards-recognitions / Contact. **Note the "Writing" taxonomy** — books / articles / op-eds / reports is a much better model for a policy-facing academic than one flat "Publications" list. Weakness: hero is `simon-lee-HmNmpnIZlU0-unsplash.jpg` — stock.

**Cecilia Baldoni** — `https://cecibaldoni.github.io/`, `<meta generator="quarto-1.10.18">`, Bootstrap 5. Colours `#fdf6ee` / `#0f3318` / `#e8c97e` / `#a3be6e`; `font-family: Roboto Mono`. **UTokyo aqua lab** — `https://aqua.t.u-tokyo.ac.jp/en/`. Avada theme + LayerSlider + WPML (`stt:1,28`). `<title>` carries the Japanese mission statement. Colours `#092289` navy, `#65bc7b` green. H2s: "Message from professors" / "INFORMATION & NEWS" / "LINK" / "Reclutes" (sic). Bilingual pattern good; everything else is stock Avada.

## E. Verified negatives / gaps

- `https://louisejslater.com/` (Louise Slater, Professor of Hydroclimatology, Oxford — the closest UK analogue to Satish) currently serves a maintenance page: H1 "We're getting things ready". Wayback has 200-snapshots at 20230531, 20240623, 20250302, 20250520 but they return gzipped raw bytes and `web.archive.org` is blocked to my rendered fetcher, so I could NOT verify its design. **UNVERIFIED — worth a manual look by a human, it is likely the single most relevant exemplar.**
- `https://brg.ethz.ch/` (Block Research Group, ETH architecture) is a Vue/Vuetify SPA; only Roboto + Material Design Icons + Font Awesome were extractable, and neither curl nor the renderer returned page content. **Design UNVERIFIED.**
- `https://gramaziokohler.arch.ethz.ch/` is a legacy hand-rolled site: Arial/Verdana/Helvetica only, `#999999`/`#000000`/`#CCCCCC`/`#333333`, `font-size` values from 9px to 25px, **no `@media` queries at all** and no viewport meta. A famous design-research group with a non-responsive 2008-era site.
- `https://hydro.iis.u-tokyo.ac.jp/~yamadai/` now serves only a bilingual "Website has moved" notice; `~hexg/` (Xiaogang He, NUS) is 404.
- `https://www.ox.ac.uk/`, `https://nus.edu.sg/`, `https://www.epfl.ch/en/` and `https://www.ashoka.edu.in/` returned no extractable font/colour system to my parser (JS-injected or CDN-split CSS) — **their type systems are UNVERIFIED here.**
- `https://gendersmartcity.com/` (Ayona Datta's ERC project microsite) returned HTTP 444 (server refused). The *pattern* of a project getting its own microsite is confirmed by its existence in her nav, but the site itself is **UNVERIFIED**.
pitfalls: WordPress page-builder stacks are instantly legible as templates. Verified: msaharia.com = Elementor 3.13 + Poppins/Quicksand; nikowanders.com = Divi 4.27 with Divi's stock blue #2ea3f2; aqua.t.u-tokyo.ac.jp = Avada + LayerSlider; hydrosense.iitd.ac.in = 'Academix' + Elementor 3.28. All four are competent scientists with sites that read as bought.

Free HTML templates with un-purged placeholder copy. akshayanikumbh.github.io still shows 'And this is a massive headline', 'interdum dolor', 'Tempus sed nulla imperdiet' and pic04–pic07.jpg. If any placeholder survives to launch it destroys credibility more thoroughly than an ugly site would.

Too many typefaces. Vimal Mishra's lab CSS loads Maven Pro, Open Sans, Source Sans Pro, Work Sans and Jost. IISc's homepage mixes Playfair Display, Roboto Condensed, Source Sans Pro and museo-sans. This is the most common way an otherwise-decent academic site reads as generic.

Bootstrap 3 / Bootstrap default blue #337ab7 and Glyphicons — still live on home.iitd.ac.in and iisc.ac.in. Also FontAwesome-as-decoration: icon fonts standing in for research imagery makes every lab site look like every other lab site.

Stock photography. Even the well-art-directed ayonadatta.com is undercut by an Unsplash hero (simon-lee-HmNmpnIZlU0-unsplash.jpg). For a hydrologist there is no excuse — field photos, gauges, drone frames and model output all exist.

Google Sites on an institutional Workspace domain can become invisible: sites.google.com/a/iitgn.ac.in/... now returns a Google sign-in wall to anonymous visitors. Do not let the CMS own the public URL.

Institutional subdomain hosting. hydrosense.iitd.ac.in serves an incomplete TLS chain (openssl verify code 21) — an automated fetcher refused it outright and some mobile clients will too. Path-hosting under iith.ac.in also guarantees URL churn when the institute redesigns.

Shipping without a viewport meta tag. Confirmed missing on civil.iitb.ac.in/~subimal/, personal.lse.ac.uk/ghatak/, gabriel-zucman.eu, statsmapsnpix.com, home.iiserb.ac.in/~kumarp/ and gramaziokohler.arch.ethz.ch. Eminence does not excuse it.

Microsoft Word 'Save as Web Page' output — still the actual state of an IIT Bombay Institute Chair Professor's site. If any legacy content is migrated by copy-paste from .doc, Word's roman/swiss/Calibri font junk and mso- styles will come with it.

Generic research-area labels ('Hydrology', 'Climate Change', 'Data Science'). Koll's 'Warm pool expansion warps MJO' and 'Increasing Arabian Sea Cyclones' are the counter-example; generic labels are the single biggest tell of a template-filled site.

Hero carousels and sliders. LayerSlider on the UTokyo lab, a hand-rolled .carousel-track on the IITH profile page. They hide content, hurt mobile, and read as 2014. Yamazaki Lab gets away with one only because every slide is its own model output.

Copying the department CMS aesthetic. ETH's Rietholzbach page — a world-famous research catchment — has zero photographs, maps or plots. European institutional pages are deliberately dry; imitating them produces a site with nothing to look at.
Letting the RAFT page become a link stub. raftwaters.in does not currently resolve, so a thin 'see our other site' page would leave the group with no public presence at all.

Designing the blog index before the blog article template. A hydrologist's posts are figure-led; if there is no proper figure-with-caption component and no wide-figure escape hatch, every post will look broken.

Cyan-blue 'water' branding. TU Delft owns #00a6d6, Divi ships #2ea3f2, and half of hydrology defaults to the same hue. Wageningen's cream/deep-green/navy and APU's ochre/maroon/cream both show better routes.

exemplars.name: Yamazaki Lab (Dai Yamazaki), Institute of Industrial Science, University of Tokyo
exemplars.what_works: GitHub Pages + Bootstrap, no CMS. The hero carousel is composed entirely of the lab's own model and dataset output (MERIT_DEM.jpg, MERIT_width.jpg, CaMa_Mekong.jpg, CaMa_model.jpg, Hillslope.jpg) rather than stock or campus photos, so the visual identity is inseparable from the science. Home flows Welcome → 'What is Global Hydrodynamics?' → Monthly Public Seminar → CaMa-Flood modelling community → 'Rainfall-Runoff Modelling Game' → Japanese section. Casual dated team photo (DLab_2024Dec.jpg) rather than a posed one. Restrained, near-monochrome, content-first.
exemplars.steal_this: Make the hero images exclusively your own model output and maps — a Musi/Godavari inundation map, a SnapFlood frame, a forecast-verification plot — and give one outreach artefact (a game, a dashboard, a Telugu explainer) a named slot on the home page.

exemplars.name: Climate Research Lab (Roxy Mathew Koll), IITM Pune
exemplars.what_works: Research navigation is written as findings, not categories: 'Increasing Arabian Sea Cyclones', 'Warm pool expansion warps MJO', 'Marine Heatwaves and Monsoon', 'Widespread Extreme Rains', 'Climate and Dengue', 'Future Indian Ocean'. 'Data Products' and 'Student Guidelines' are promoted to top-level nav. The news section is a wall of scanned newspaper op-eds and interviews including Telugu (Eenadu) and Malayalam (Mathrubhumi) outlets — an authenticity signal no template can produce. Sage #bdcc96 is the only real colour; the figures and clippings carry everything.
exemplars.steal_this: Name research areas as claims, put 'Data & Products' and 'For students' in the top nav, and build a press wall from real Indian and regional-language clippings with outlet + date.

exemplars.name: Water and Climate Lab (Vimal Mishra), IIT Gandhinagar
exemplars.what_works: The most complete IA I found for an Indian hydro-climate PI, extracted from its React bundle: four named research themes (climate-and-urban-systems, climate-extremes-understanding, hydrologic-monitoring-and-prediction, hydrologic-sensitivity-and-change); publications split four ways (journal-articles / books-expository-and-review-articles / conference-presentations / invited-papers); people split four ways (current / alumni / interns / gallery); plus first-class /data and /data-portals routes. Navy #003b75 with cyan #00aeef.
exemplars.steal_this: Adopt this exact route skeleton — four research themes, four publication types, four people categories, data as a top-level section — but implement it with ONE font family instead of its five (Maven Pro + Work Sans + Jost + Source Sans Pro + Open Sans is why it feels templated).

exemplars.name: HydroSense Lab (Manabendra Saharia), IIT Delhi
exemplars.what_works: Nearest peer institution and nearest research area (floods, landslides, hydrologic forecasting, geospatial AI). Near-monochrome black / #EDF2F6 with a single red accent #D30015; Montserrat 400/500/700 for headings over Open Sans. Funder logo strip sits immediately under the hero (ISRO, MoES, MoRD, DST, PSA, CDRI, IC-IMPACTS, Sony). Research shown as four image cards; 'Lab Updates' feed; 'Products' and 'Awards & Impact' as separate top-level items.
exemplars.steal_this: The funder/collaborator logo strip directly under the hero, and the single-accent discipline. Also learn from its failure: it runs on the Academix WP theme and an IITD subdomain with a broken TLS chain (openssl verify code 21) — own your domain and hosting.

exemplars.name: Climate Lab Book / Show Your Stripes (Ed Hawkins), University of Reading
exemplars.what_works: Two figures the author made — 'Climate spirals' and 'Warming stripes' — are permanent top-level navigation items alongside Home/About/Contact, and one of them spun out into its own site (https://showyourstripes.info/, Vue + Vuetify + Roboto, neutral greys). Data graphics, not photographs, do all the visual work; the blog is the spine and the figures are the brand.
exemplars.steal_this: Promote your single most recognisable figure to a permanent nav item with its own page ('Urban flooding in Hyderabad', 'The Godavari forecast') instead of burying it in a paper list — one figure elevated to identity is worth more than a redesign.

exemplars.name: Danny Dorling, School of Geography and the Environment, University of Oxford
exemplars.what_works: Every news item leads with a 'Featured graphic' — a map or chart image, never a portrait (Featured_graphic-5.png, FeaturedGraphic-1-1024x653.jpg). Lora serif for the name and headings over Muli/Roboto UI, red accent #ff1f55. Home sections are News / Recent Books / 'What other people say' — the last being third-party quotes about his work instead of a self-written bio.
exemplars.steal_this: Image-first news cards where the image is always a map or figure, and a 'what others say' block (press quotes, award citations, testimonials) in place of a second self-description.

exemplars.name: Ayona Datta, Department of Geography, UCL
exemplars.what_works: An editorial magazine register achieved with CSS overrides on Squarespace: Playfair Display via Typekit, 1.5px solid-black bottom rules instead of input boxes, uppercase micro-labels at .1–.2em tracking, 2px black ghost buttons that invert on hover, navy #16263c. Writing is taxonomised as Books / Journal Articles and Book Chapters / Op-eds / Reports / Blog, and Speaking as Keynotes / Multimedia / Media & Press / Upcoming Talks.
exemplars.steal_this: The Writing taxonomy (papers vs op-eds vs reports vs blog) — exactly right for a hydrologist who writes policy notes and public pieces — plus hairline rules and uppercase tracked micro-labels instead of cards and shadows.

exemplars.name: Cecilia Baldoni (Best Interactive Website, Personal Academic Websites Contest 2025)
exemplars.what_works: Built with Quarto 1.10.18 — a plain static generator — yet looks entirely bespoke because the home page is one hand-drawn SVG cityscape (ceci-city.svg) whose buildings are the navigation, backed by a matching custom icon set (research, illustrations, talks-workshops, open-science, bookshop, radio, van, coffee-kiosk). Palette cream #fdf6ee, forest #0f3318, gold #e8c97e, sage #a3be6e; Roboto Mono.
exemplars.steal_this: One commissioned or hand-made illustration/diagram used as the site's organising image beats any premium theme. For a hydrologist the natural version is a stylised catchment/river-network schematic whose nodes are the sections (headwaters → forecast → city → people).

exemplars.name: Our World in Data (Global Change Data Lab / University of Oxford)
exemplars.what_works: The canonical data-forward type and colour system: exactly one family, Lato, self-hosted in eight weights plus italics (Hairline through Black), over a single tinted navy scale — #1d3d63, #426591, #577291, #a4b6ca, #dbe5f0, #ebeef2 — with one red #ce261e for emphasis. Nothing decorative; all differentiation comes from weight, size and tint.
exemplars.steal_this: One family + eight weights + one hue scale + one accent. This is the cheapest possible route to a site that looks systematically designed rather than assembled, and it suits figure-heavy pages.

exemplars.name: Wageningen University & Research (institutional palette reference)
exemplars.what_works: A land-and-water institution that refuses corporate blue: cream grounds #FBF6E5 and #F3ECD3, deep greens #004D00 and #153816, navy #002B47, dark red #661118, soft pink #FFAAAE. Warm and earthy, reads as agronomy and hydrology rather than software.
exemplars.steal_this: The cream-ground + deep-green + navy + one-dark-red combination as an alternative to the IITH amber route — it sits naturally with field photography, satellite imagery and terrain maps, and pairs well with IITH's existing #FDFBF8 background.

exemplars.name: Azim Premji University, Bengaluru
exemplars.what_works: Proof that an Indian institution can look contemporary without looking imported: Source Sans 3 variable (200–900 with italics) on Tailwind, over ochre #c76815, deep maroon #771d1d and cream #fef6d6. The warmth is sub-continental; the execution is current.
exemplars.steal_this: The ochre/maroon/cream register as the 'Indian but internationally credible' palette — it also happens to be close to IITH's own #fa9110 / #d1402a / #FDFBF8.

exemplars.name: IIT Hyderabad faculty profile — Satish Kumar Regonda (institutional anchor)
exemplars.what_works: IITH's own system, which is better than most Indian institutes': self-hosted Frutiger LT Pro in five cuts, warm off-white body #FDFBF8, text #333333, amber #D97706 / #fa9110 and brick #d1402a, on Tailwind + Alpine. Research interests are already listed as eight items (Urban and Rural Flood Modeling, Climate Sciences, Data Sciences, Statistical Modeling Techniques, Ensemble Forecasting, Multiscale Modelling, AI/ML, Climate Change).
exemplars.steal_this: Inherit #FDFBF8, #333333 and the amber/brick accent so the personal site reads as an extension of IITH rather than a foreign object — then diverge on typography (a humanist sans in the Frutiger lineage: Inter, Source Sans 3 or Figtree) since Frutiger LT Pro is licensed.

exemplars.name: Alasdair Rae — Stats, Maps n Pix (formerly University of Sheffield, geography)
exemplars.what_works: A stock Blogger template where every post thumbnail is a square 400×400 map (green-belt-pop-2021.png, building-area-vs-pop.png, uprn-vs-buildings.png). Open Sans, #444444 text, green #160 links. Zero design budget, enormous readership — the maps are the entire design.
exemplars.steal_this: A strict square crop for every blog/news thumbnail, always a map or chart. Consistency of shape plus consistency of content type produces a grid that looks designed even when nothing else is.

exemplars.name: Fawad Ahmed Najam (NUST Pakistan → UBC Okanagan) — Best Educational Resource Website 2025
exemplars.what_works: A South Asian engineering academic whose site is organised around teaching artefacts rather than a CV: named course pages (CE 809 Structural Dynamics Fall 2021/2020, CE 416 Earthquake Engineering Spring 2020), video lecture series as home-page features, and long-form technical blog posts answering specific student questions ('Why building codes require a base shear scaling for the RSA procedure?'). Blue #015389, teal #009e9e, green #96c346.
exemplars.steal_this: Structure Teaching as durable, linkable course pages with materials, and let the blog answer concrete technical questions from students and practitioners — for Satish, flood-forecast verification, R/Shiny and Google Earth Engine how-tos, which he already teaches.
